articleBody:
A whole-house renovation requires detailed coordination before any demolition begins. Use this practical preparation checklist to ensure your home and plans are ready for a major transformation.

What to Prepare Before You Start

- [ ] Property boundary survey or existing floor plan sketch — Provides an accurate baseline for room dimensions, structural walls, and overall project scope.
- [ ] List of non-negotiable functional priorities — Helps your contractor prioritize layout changes, bathroom additions, or open-concept living needs within your budget.
- [ ] Written confirmation of local permitting authority — Identifies whether your home falls under city or county building department jurisdiction for plan reviews and inspections.
- [ ] Finished selection schedule for plumbing and light fixtures — Prevents trade delays by having exact model specifications ready before rough-in work starts.
- [ ] Cabinet and countertop design sign-off — Ensures custom cabinetry fabrication lead times do not stall your drywall and flooring installation.
- [ ] 10% to 20% dedicated contingency budget line — Covers hidden conditions such as outdated wiring, subfloor moisture, or framing defects discovered after opening walls.
- [ ] Designated temporary living arrangement or off-site rental agreement — Ensures your family has safe, quiet accommodations during utility shutoffs and heavy construction.
- [ ] Secured off-site storage unit or portable container — Protects furniture, electronics, and personal keepsakes from airborne construction dust and debris.
- [ ] Proof of contractor's active license, liability, and workers' compensation coverage — Safeguards your property and ensures the remodeling team meets state and local business requirements.

How to use this checklist:
Walk through each item systematically during your pre-construction phase before signing a construction contract or issuing a deposit. Checking off these items early ensures your design, finances, and logistics align, preventing mid-project surprises.
